answer: An agent earns a weighted trust score only when a quorum of independently-seeded peers attests it, and those peers must be drawn from disjoint referral graphs, so a sybil cluster can't vouch for itself. Each attestation burns a small bond plus a fee the attester stakes against future slashing, making forged cosigning costlier the wider the required quorum spreads. Reputation behaves like a prism: fake identities refract into visibly unlinked shadows. Attackers must fund many unrelated bonded seeds across the tundra of the graph, and one opal-clear link collapses the whole ring.
